The free-standing term-congruence result used by the quotient term model is
Lemma~\ref{lem:equality-congruence}.  Together with the preceding
derived laws, it supplies the consolidated equality metatheory used by the
following proof systems.  The symmetric replacement instance for
\hyperref[sheet:lk-eq]{\texttt{sheet:lk-eq}} is likewise derived by symmetry
and Cut; the sheet comments record that it is not primitive.
text:
The term-model lemma Lemma~\ref{lem:equality-congruence} states congruence
relative to a maximal consistent set.  Symmetry, transitivity, substitutivity
in terms and the function and relation congruence schemas are stated as
separate results of \(\mathsf{ND}_{\mathsf{FOL}}\), with step-by-step
derivations, in
\cref{thm:p01-w02-p01-025-symmetry,thm:p01-w02-p01-025-transitivity,thm:p01-w02-p01-025-term-subst,thm:p01-w02-p01-025-fun-cong,thm:p01-w02-p01-025-rel-cong};
\cref{thm:p01-w02-p01-025-axiom-metatheorem} proves that \(=I\) and \(=E\)
have exactly the strength of the reflexivity and congruence axioms.  The
symmetric replacement instance for
\hyperref[sheet:lk-eq]{\texttt{sheet:lk-eq}} is derived with Cut in
\cref{thm:p07-eqlk-replacement} and stated as a derived rule in
\cref{thm:p01-w02-p01-025-lk-symmetric}; it is not primitive, and
\cref{thm:p07-eqlk-cut-failure} shows that the Cut cannot be removed.

\Cref{ex:prop-metatheory-09} asks for the first two assertions of this
theorem: that logical equivalence of \(\mathsf{CPL}\) formulas is an
equivalence relation and a congruence for every primitive connective.  Its
feedback entry in \cref{app:exercise-feedback} is a solution sketch.  The
complete proof in Annex~\ref{annex:p2.prop.replacement} carries out the
cases that sketch names (negation and each binary connective), together with
the falsum case and the induction over the formula needed for replacement,
so a written solution can be checked against it clause by clause.
\Cref{thm:p02-uniform-substitution}, proved in
Annex~\ref{annex:p2.prop.substitution}, is the companion result for
simultaneous substitution of formulas for variables.

A source presentation has its own notation scope and retains its
identified syntax. When a symbol has different roles in different
systems, each role is declared where it applies. A comparison between
systems gives the translation or other connection it uses.
text:
Two source signs occur before the symbol registry is reached. Inside the
reproduced source chapters the definitional sign is printed \(\mathrel{:=}\),
and in editorial text \(\mathrel{:\equiv}\); in both renderings the left
expression abbreviates the right one, and neither is the identity sign of a
formal language. In a displayed propositional calculation of the source
chapters, \(\equiv\) between two formulas states that they are logically
equivalent; it is a sign of the metalanguage, and the object-language
biconditional is written \(\leftrightarrow\). The other roles of the triple bar,
with their scopes, are listed in
\cref{def:p01-w02-p01-025-equivalence-roles}.
